page: Google Cloud Platform m2-hypermem-416 is an ultra-high-capacity virtual machine in the Memory Optimized family, architected for workloads requiring extraordinary memory footprints. It is driven by Intel Xeon x86_64 processors with 208 physical cores supporting 416 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 8,832 GB of system memory, establishing a generous allocation ratio of 21.23 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators, operating entirely on persistent network storage and standard CPU instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded and memory throughput metrics alongside clear single-thread limitations. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations exceeding 300 million operations per second. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 659.2 GB/s, with write bandwidth sustaining 314.85 GB/s. Conversely, single-core metrics in Geekbench and gzip compression test in the bottom quartiles, reflecting the tradeoff of dense multi-socket Intel architectures optimized for horizontal parallel throughput rather than peak per-core frequency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m2-hypermem-416 is structured to maximize resource density, allowing enterprises to consolidate multi-node database clusters into a single unified memory address space to minimize cluster management overhead and interconnect latency. It is specifically targeted for hyperscale in-memory databases, large SAP HANA production environments, distributed memory caching engines, and complex enterprise analytics processing vast active datasets.
description: Google Cloud Platform m2-hypermem-416 is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to the Memory Optimized machine family, designed for exceptionally large data-intensive architectures. It is powered by 208 physical cores and 416 vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon platform operating at 2.7 GHz, backed by 8,832 GB of system memory, providing approximately 21.23 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network-attached storage volumes. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-threaded capabilities, with exceptional stress-ng multi-core scores, extensive uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 650 GB/s, and high-frequency in-memory key-value processing reaching over 300 million Redis operations per second. However, single-core processing remains weak due to modest base clock frequencies. Given its immense memory density, m2-hypermem-416 delivers high cost efficiency for consolidating distributed in-memory platforms, making it optimal for large SAP HANA deployments, massive in-memory databases, and high-concurrency business intelligence analytics.
